text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein, French President Chirac to discuss developments in Middle East peace process; French ambassador says Paris values king's role in Washington summit.
- Continued consultations between Jordanian and Palestinian leaderships; king praises "flexibility and patience of the Palestinian negotiator".
- Memorandum of understanding between government and state medical staff on their demands; raises in extra allowances for doctors, nurses and pharmacists.
- Prime Minister Kabariti tours Sports City to examine damage at soccer game after trouble broke out in Friday's match; expresses regret at damage.
- Under directives from King Hussein, consignment of drugs and medicines sent from health ministry as donation to Palestinian Authority.
- Phone consultations between King Hussein and Palestinian President Arafat to coordinate positions in support of Palestinian negotiator.
- Social Security Corporation plans setting up comprehensive industrial city and investing in electric generation.
- Union of electricity workers suspends stoppage.
- Important speech by Chirac in parliament on Thursday; opposition deputies decide on Sunday whether to attend or boycott.
- National outrage at troubles in Sports City, 14 people injured and damage to 24 buses and 35,000 dinars losses.
- Kabariti takes part in funeral procession for four Badia (border police) forces killed in car accident.
- Large fire in textiles plant; loss of a million dinars; technical committee on incident begins work on Sunday.
